question.problem:
A cellphone battery's average time from full to empty is $26$ hours. Additionally, $20%$ of the time, the battery lasts less than $20$ hours. Assuming that the duration of the battery is normally distributed, find the percentage of the times that a full charge lasts more than $30$ hours, rounded to $1$ decimal place.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.10\,$ | $\,0.15\,$ | $\,0.20\,$ | $\,0.25\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ | $\,-1.8808\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-1.0364\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6736\,$ | $\,0.6772\,$ | $\,0.6808\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.7088\,$ | $\,0.7123\,$ | $\,0.7157\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7422\,$ | $\,0.7454\,$ | $\,0.7486\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the time a full charge lasts. Then we have $X∼N(26,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X>30).$ But first, we need to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X<20)=0.20.$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<20) & =0.20 \\ P(Z\le \frac{20-26}{\sigma }) & =0.20 \\ Φ(\frac{-6}{\sigma }) & =0.20 \\ \frac{-6}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.20)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.20)≈-0.8416.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-6}{\sigma } & =-0.8416 \\ \frac{1}{\sigma } & =0.14027 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{1}{0.14027} \\  & ≈7.1291.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(30<X)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>30) & =P(Z>\frac{30-26}{7.1291}) \\  & ≈P(Z>0.56) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.56) \\  & =1-Φ(0.56) \\  & =1-0.7123 \\  & ≈28.8%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $28.8%$ of the times the battery lasts more than $30$ hours.
